instruction: Fully configure VLC to allow running multiple independent instances — disable both the general single-instance lock and the file manager single-instance option.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

trajectory_guidance.original_instruction:
I want to watch two or more videos in same time on VLC. I tried to run multiple instances of VLC. It worked but can't play videos on those new instances. When I play video it plays on first instance instead of new instance.
Is there any way to solve this problem?

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VLC Tools > Preferences, found the 'Playlist and Instances' section, unchecked 'Use only one instance when started from file manager', and saved. The 'Allow only one instance' checkbox was also visible.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VLC Preferences, locate Playlist and Instances section, toggle checkboxes, and save settings.
metadata.task_rationale: Hardened version of the original task requiring the agent to disable BOTH single-instance settings: 'Allow only one instance' (one-instance=0) and 'Use only one instance when started from file manager' (one-instance-when-started-from-file=0). Screenshot 2 showed both checkboxes, so the agent can see and interact with both.
metadata.explanation: The custom getter reads vlcrc and extracts both 'one-instance' and 'one-instance-when-started-from-file' values. The metric awards 0.5 for each setting being 0. The initial state has one-instance-when-started-from-file=1 (enabled), providing negative-control resistance for that sub-goal.

scoring_breakdown.one_instance_from_file_disabled: 0.5 - 'Use only one instance when started from file manager' is 0

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads both VLC single-instance settings from vlcrc using grep with an extended regex that matches exactly 'one-instance=' and 'one-instance-when-started-from-file=' (no overlap).
Getter properly handles both commented (default) and uncommented (user-set) config lines, preferring uncommented values — this correctly captures both written and default settings.
Metric awards 0.5 per sub-goal (one-instance==0 and one-instance-when-started-from-file==0), fully covering both requirements stated in the instruction.
postconfig kills VLC then restarts it, ensuring vlcrc is flushed to disk before the getter reads it — this is the correct pattern for VLC preference verification.
Negative control resistance is present: initial state has one-instance-when-started-from-file=1, so the do-nothing baseline scores at most 0.5, not 1.0.
Error handling in metric (returns 0.0 on missing/errored result dict) prevents false positives.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The metric hardcodes comparison to '0' rather than reading from the expected dict (keys one_instance_expected / one_instance_from_file_expected). This is functionally correct for this task but reduces reusability. Consider reading expected values from the passed 'expected' parameter for robustness.
